b2-19-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Across the Plain
b2-19-01.scenario: In the story, a young writer (Gyula) looks over the estate with an old farmhand. A visitor asks you to describe what lies on each side of the river that the story mentions.
b2-19-01.prompt: Tell the visitor what is on this side of the river and what is beyond it.
cues: Say what is on this side
Say what is beyond the river
b2-19-01.target: A folyón innen dombok vannak, a folyón túl nagy síkság terül el.
b2-19-01.english: On this side of the river there are hills, beyond the river a big plain stretches out.
b2-19-01.canDo: I can delineate geographic and symbolic boundaries using innen and túl

b2-19-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Along the Cottages
b2-19-02.scenario: A visitor asks you where the farmhands' white houses stand in the story's estate.
b2-19-02.prompt: Tell the visitor where the houses are and how far the avenue of trees goes.
cues: Say how far the avenue goes
b2-19-02.target: A cselédházak az út mentén állnak, és a fasor végig az úton halad.
b2-19-02.english: The farmhands' houses stand along the road, and the avenue of trees runs all along the road.
b2-19-02.canDo: I can trace continuous trajectories along entire routes using végig

b2-19-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Up to the Capital
b2-19-03.scenario: Gyula, the young writer in the story, asks you where young people from the countryside go and where city families go.
b2-19-03.prompt: Tell Gyula where the young people go and where some city families move.
cues: Say where some city families move
b2-19-03.target: A fiatalok felutaznak a fővárosba, de néhány városi család kiköltözik a tanyára.
b2-19-03.english: Young people travel up to the capital, but some city families move out to a farmstead.
b2-19-03.canDo: I can use conventional Hungarian directional preverbs (fel/le, ki/be) to contrast capital and provinces

b2-19-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Which Region?
b2-19-04.scenario: A guest at the estate asks you about two regions of Hungary, the Great Plain and the Bakony.
b2-19-04.prompt: Tell your guest what you can find in each region.
cues: Say what the Great Plain has
b2-19-04.target: Az Alföldön nagy síkság van, a Bakonyban pedig sok erdő.
b2-19-04.english: On the Great Plain there is a big plain, and in the Bakony there are many forests.
b2-19-04.canDo: I can select appropriate case endings (-on/-en/-ön vs. -ban/-ben) for Hungarian geographical regions

b2-19-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Farmhand Feels
b2-19-05.scenario: Gyula, the young writer, asks you what the old farmhand in the story says about the land.
b2-19-05.prompt: Tell Gyula what the farmhand says about the land.
cues: Say what the farmhand does not have
Say how he feels about the land
b2-19-05.target: Az öreg béres azt mondja, hogy nincs saját földjük, de úgy érzik, hogy a föld az övék.
b2-19-05.english: The old farmhand says they have no land of their own, but they feel that the land is theirs.
b2-19-05.canDo: I can describe the life of the manorial servants and their bond with the land as the story shows it

b2-19-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Banks, One Land
b2-19-consolidation.scenario: A visitor to the estate asks you to sum up the land around the river: both banks and the villages along it.
b2-19-consolidation.prompt: Tell the visitor what the land is like on both banks and what the villages keep.
cues: Say what is on this side of the river
b2-19-consolidation.target: A folyón innen dombok vannak, a folyón túl nagy síkság, és szerte a vidéken sok falu őrzi a régi hagyományokat.
b2-19-consolidation.english: On this side of the river there are hills, beyond it a big plain, and all over the region many villages keep the old traditions.
b2-19-consolidation.canDo: I can navigate spatial postpositions (innen, túl, szerte, mentén, táján, végig) with confidence
